subject: Reduce item levels using GRM item parameters

messages.author: eab9582ba50c948a
messages.subject: Reduce item levels using GRM item parameters
parts:
Hi there,

I've calculated a unidimensional GRM of a test and would like to evaluate and reduce the (theoretically proposed) item levels. For instance, I got the following IRCCC of an item with 3 levels:
it's clear, that level 2 is redundant, but do I replace those responses with level 1 or better level 3? Can I use the item parameters to decide this? They are

$WPO_9C
          a1       d1        d2
par 1.431 -0.004 -0.859

even more difficult, I've got this item (and some similar more) with 5 levels, where I think, I can omit level 2 to 4:
$WPO_8B
         a1       d1       d2      d3       d4
par 1.509 0.889 0.619 0.252 -0.692

What do I do here? Or do I just combine the item levels visually, from the IRCCC graph? Or just split them arithmetically?

I tried to research this question but didn't find good articles about it, I'm glad for help there, too!

Thanks for your expertise, Martin

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Reduce item levels using GRM item parameters
parts:
Collapsing categories in the context of the GRM will ultimately lead to less information about the measurement of the latent trait, so you could try to justify this perspective from a measurement information context. Personally, I tend to only collapse categories when there is insufficient information available (e.g., like 5 responses for a given Likert scale option) or when the response itself is questionable in the context of measurement (in which case the removal is more diagnostic and justifiable at a theoretical level). 

Anytime you change data around there are consequences, with varying intensity, so it would indeed be difficult to find "hard rules" on the topic in the literature (rules of thumb, maybe, though honestly some rules of thumb feel like there's been a carpentry accident on the side of the authors ....). 

Phil
